{"content":"An unchanged calendar value can reverse another editor's move. If one Save moves an event from A to B, the queue reloads the event from B. A queued title-only draft still contains calendarId A. Save selects A and moves the event back. A queued occurrence edit can instead fail the move-permission check.","codeSuggestion":"","assessment":"P2. Save treats an unchanged calendar as an explicit move request.","rationale":"applyCalendarEventDraft compares title and date values with the baseline. Calendar selection has no equivalent comparison before event.calendar is assigned at line 121. test_overlappingEditsAfterCalendarMove changes the calendar in both drafts. test_queuedOccurrencesFollowWholeSeriesShifts also changes every draft calendar in its move case.","recommendation":"change","validation":"Executed the current Save, queue, loader, field helpers, and draft/session reducers with controlled calendars, events, and transactions. Both requests succeeded. The transactions were A to B, then B to A. The explicit-B control produced A to B, then B to B. No Thunderbird runtime test ran.","appliedSummary":"Updated [Save](mail/components/calendar/content/calendar-event-edit-save.mjs) to preserve the reloaded calendar when the draft calendar is unchanged. Explicit moves remain supported.

Added [regression tests](mail/components/calendar/test/unit/test_calendarEventEditSave.js) for queued title and occurrence edits, including Undo.

Lint, syntax, whitespace, and controlled checks passed. The xpcshell test remains unrun because build source stamps are unknown. The diff follows the recorded evidence; no exact accepted Save example was found.

Changes remain unstaged and uncommitted.","changeSummary":"Use the reloaded calendar when draft.calendarId matches baseline.calendarId. Preserve explicit moves.
